literature.cite: Boeken, P., O. Zoeter and J. M. Mooij, 2025: Conditional Forecasts and Proper Scoring Rules for Reliable and Accurate Performative Predictions. arXiv:2510.21335v1.
literature.read: abstract only, through a page-to-text fetch on 2026-10-16
passages: Performative predictions are forecasts which influence the outcomes they aim to predict,
However, even under this condition, classical proper scoring rules fail to elicit correct forecasts.
literature.use: the theory's side: a forecast that changes its outcome is not elicited correctly by a proper score; this study prices the gap in one record

handoff.offer: a proper score charges a heeded warning (p*e)^2 per occasion, so scoring tornado warnings on deaths fines the ones that worked

searches: one web search for scoring warnings that prevent their own outcome, 2026-10-16: no measurement of the fine's size in a real warning record found (about my search)
